title: llm-routing-prefetch-rough-prd-scratchpad-ethan-walker
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick scratchpad for a possible feature: 'Adaptive KV-prefetch + routing' (working title).
- Goal: reduce tail latency and token cost for common interactive chat flows by prefetching KV-cache for likely next-turn contexts and routing to cheaper model variants when confidence is high.
- This is a user-level brainstorming doc: rough PRD outline, user stories, risks, basic acceptance criteria, and engineering notes. Not polished.

Problem statement (as I see it):
- Many prod chat workloads have predictable conversational patterns (FAQ, onboarding flows, templated responses).
- Cold KV-cache and small batch sizes -> higher per-token latency and cost.
- We have model variants (quantized/fast) that are cheaper but sometimes lower quality on edge cases.
- Need an approach that: prefetches KV state when safe, routes requests to cheaper model when confidence is ok, and falls back gracefully.

Hypothesis:
- If we prefetch KV-cache for the most likely next tokens/positions and route low-risk requests to a cheaper variant, we can reduce median latency by ~15-30% and token cost by 10-25% without measurable UX regression on typical flows.

High-level feature idea (components):
1) KV-prefetch policy engine (runtime + config):
   - Runs a lightweight predictor on incoming request to estimate next-turn prefix probability distribution (e.g., next N tokens or next-turn template id).
   - For high-probability prefixes, pre-warm KV-cache on the target serving nodes (or use shared cache layer).
   - Configurable TTL / staleness window for prefetched KV.
2) Confidence-based routing policy:
   - Score each incoming request for suitability to a cheaper model variant (quantized or lower-capacity).
   - If score > threshold AND relevant KV prefetched, route to fast variant.
   - If model indicates low confidence at generation time (or failing eval checks), fallback to primary model and optionally warm its KV.
3) Observability + guardrails:
   - Track per-route metrics: latency P50/P95, cost per token, changed answer rate (A/B against baseline), failure/fallback rates.
   - Alerting for quality regressions (deviations in rerank metrics / user-reported errors).

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer for onboarding chat, I want the system to reduce token cost for predictable flows so we can keep our pricing low.
- As an SRE, I want prefetching to not cause bursty spikes in GPU utilization (configurable max prefetch concurrency).
- As an ML infra engineer, I want strict rollback if fallback rate crosses X% so we preserve SLAs.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Safety: No silent quality regressions. Define metric: "changed-answer-rate" + human eval sample must be <= baseline delta (0.5% preliminary).
- Performance: For selected onboarding route, median latency reduced by >= 15% and token compute cost reduced by >= 10% in canary.
- Reliability: Prefetch operations should not increase GPU utilization by more than 20% during steady-state.

Open questions / risks:
- How to predict next-turn tokens reliably without expensive model compute? Options: tiny next-step predictor (N-gram / small LSTM / distilled model) vs heuristics (route id, templates).
- Prefetch cache storage model: per-node KV warming vs shared prefix cache service (tradeoffs: memory overhead vs cross-node hits).
- Security/data isolation: ensure prefetch does not leak sensitive conversation context across customers when running shared caches. Need tenant-aware tagging.
- Cost of false prefetching: wasted GPU cycles vs benefit. Need good TTL and adaptive backoff.
- How to measure quality regressions at scale? Need automated eval harness and periodic human sampling.

Implementation sketch / tech notes:
- Start with a narrow canary: one route (onboarding flow) with high repeatability and owned by growth/product.
- Predictor prototype: train small classifier on historical chats to map current-turn to likely next-turn template id (top-K). Use that to prefetch the corresponding KV tokens.
- Routing: reuse existing smart routing layer; add a per-request header flag (candidate_fast_variant=true) and a scoring hook that consults predictor + policy.
- Prefetch mechanism: add an async prefetch API to the serving runtime that can load KV into GPU memory without blocking the request path. Must expose limits (max concurrent prefetches, memory budget).
- Fallback: synchronous fallback to primary model if generation probability distribution deviates (or special exception). Ensure tracing shows why fallback happened.

Metrics to collect (initial):
- Prefetch hit rate (prefetched KV used / prefetched ops)
- Prefetch wasted rate (prefetched but not used within TTL)
- Per-route latency P50/P95, before/after
- Token compute cost per route (cost units)
- Fallback rate and reasons
- Quality signals: changed-answer-rate, human eval pass rate

Experiment plan (canary -> ramp):
- Phase 0: offline analysis on historical logs. Build predictor, compute theoretical hit rates and cost tradeoffs.
- Phase 1: internal canary on staging infra for selected route. Measure prefetch mechanics, memory usage, and safety.
- Phase 2: 5% production traffic for route, monitor metrics & quality. If stable, 25%, then 100%.

TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Sync with Priya (product) and Jordan (runtime) — schedule 30m sync.
- [ ] Run quick offline analysis: top-10 routes by repeatability + cost; estimate top-K next-turn hit rates. (Assigned: Ethan)
- [ ] Prototype tiny predictor model and evaluate accuracy on sample of 10k chats. (Assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Spike: implement a non-blocking prefetch API stub in runtime to measure memory impact. (Assigned: Jordan)

Notes / rough priorities:
- Focus on high-repeatability routes first (onboarding, billing FAQ, password reset flows).
- Must instrument heavy observability before any rollout (can't rely on manual checks).
- Emphasize safe defaults: prefetch off by default per route; explicit opt-in.

References / inspiration:
- Some prior internal notes: confluence link above (prefetch design)
- Related work: "prefix caching" drafts from cache-team PRD (see linked PR)

Misc thoughts (brain dump):
- Could combine with model-aware quantization: if predictor is extremely confident, route to quantized+prefetched variant; otherwise, use smaller batch-size on baseline model.
- Maybe expose a developer API/hint: customers can tag routes as "templated" so prefetch policy is more aggressive.
- Consider a global budget token: prefetch budget per-customer/day to limit cost exposure.

End of scratchpad.

(Will convert to a milestoned PRD if we get signal from offline analysis + product.)
